header: The plug for sending a one-time code. No SMS or e-mail gateway is set up for this app, so there is nothing real to send with: I say so plainly here instead of pretending, and the feature stays off (PASSWORD_OTP). To switch it on later: write the `send` of a gateway here (the plant's SMS service, or SMTP for e-mail), keep the credentials in the host's environment (never in a file), then set PASSWORD_OTP=on. For a developer's own machine only: PASSWORD_OTP_DEV_ECHO=true prints the code in the server's console (refused when NODE_ENV is production).

symbols.name: notConfiguredSender
symbols.sig: const notConfiguredSender: OtpSender = { async send() { throw new OtpNotConfigured(); } }

symbols.name: consoleSender
symbols.sig: const consoleSender: OtpSender = { async send(d: Destination, message: string) { console.info(`[otp:dev] to ${d.channel}:${d.to} -> ${message}`); } }

symbols.sig: export function senderFromEnv(env: { PASSWORD_OTP_DEV_ECHO?: string; NODE_ENV?: string }): OtpSender
